cards.title: Potts-like minimum vertex graph coloring objective
cards.role: Defines the business problem: reward assigned colors and penalize equal colors on adjacent vertices.

checks.reason: The expression and B much greater than A interpretation are printed in Eq. (2) and the following paragraph.
Exact enumeration verifies that with one local color per vertex and B>A, any equal-color edge is penalized and every decoded target is a proper coloring.

cards.numerical_form: Use integer local states as colors; validate every decoded assignment by checking color[u] != color[v] for each graph edge.

cards.title: Multilevel Rydberg-qudit Hamiltonian

source_refs.value: Appendix A.1-A.2 C6, Omega and Delta tables

cards.role: Maps atom coordinates and one Omega/Delta/Phi channel per Rydberg level to the simulated many-body dynamics.

checks.reason: All drive, detuning, intra-level and inter-level terms are transcribed from Eq. (3); source parameter tables are frozen with the case.
The drive matrices are real symmetric, all projectors are diagonal, and the inter-level C6 matrix is explicitly symmetric, so H equals its adjoint.
Omega and Delta are converted from 2pi MHz to rad/us; C6 is converted from 2pi GHz um^6 to rad/us um^6 before division by R^6.

cards.numerical_form: Enumerate the local basis |g>,|r1>,...,|rk>; precompute pairwise diagonal C6/R^6 energies and sparse |g><->|ri> drive matrices.
open_questions: The public Pasqal/Pulser qubit model has only one Rydberg level per atom and is therefore not an equivalent backend for this Hamiltonian.

cards.title: Encoding interval under finite negative inter-level interactions
cards.role: Defines when physical spacing and detuning preserve the intended graph-coloring ground-state ordering.

checks.reason: The lower and upper bounds and maximum-degree factor are printed in Eq. (4).
Full-spectrum enumeration retains finite negative inter-level terms and reproduces the paper's loss of robustness for non-equidistant and k=chi-1 appendix cases.

cards.numerical_form: Evaluate all source C6/R^6 terms rather than replacing them by a binary blockade graph; report failures instead of clipping negative interactions.
open_questions: Figure 7 protocol-c has inconsistent Omega values between the caption extraction and Appendix A.2, so that target remains blocked.

cards.title: Normalized annealing schedules and time propagation
cards.role: Provides the five-knot Omega/Delta/Phi handoff and the 8.4 us numerical execution path.

checks.reason: Eqs. (5)-(6) give the piecewise schedules and Sec. 4.3 gives ti=0.4 us, tf=8.0 us, T=8.4 us and 300 samples.
Both schedule branches agree at ti and tf: Omega is continuous at 1 and Delta is continuous at -1 and +1.
Sparse exponential propagation preserves state norm within the recorded final numerical tolerance for every executed graph/profile.

cards.numerical_form: Use the 300 author time samples and left-endpoint piecewise-constant expm_multiply propagation from |gg...g>; phi_i(t)=0 for the printed real drives.
